questions.heading: Whether the Solver Updates in Place Depends on the Solver and the Edit
questions.stem: A service keeps one mathopt.IncrementalSolver on HiGHS (OR-Tools 9.15) and, between solves, changes one row's limit. What happens at the next solve?

options.text: HiGHS applies the new limit to the model it holds and searches on
options.says: In the runner HiGHS rebuilt after every edit, including a bound change; it applied none in place.

options.text: The solve raises, since HiGHS refuses edits between solves
options.says: Nothing is raised: MathOpt builds a new solver from the whole model and the solve goes on.

options.text: The solve uses the old limit, since the edit was made after the solver was built
options.says: The edit always reaches the next solve, by update or by rebuild; the result is right either way.

options.text: MathOpt rebuilds the HiGHS solver from the whole model, without a message
options.says: Right: HiGHS reports it cannot apply the update, and IncrementalSolver.solve() builds a new solver silently.

questions.heading: Undo Every Edit, and Never Delete What a Scenario Only Switches Off
questions.stem: A scenario loop runs row.upper_bound *= 0.9 for each of three scenarios labeled '10% cut', never restoring the row. The row started at 1,000. What limit does the third scenario solve with?

options.text: 729, since each cut applies to the limit the last one left
options.says: Right: 1,000 x 0.9 x 0.9 x 0.9 = 729, a 27.1% cut run under a 10% label, with no error.

options.text: 900, since each scenario starts from the model as built
options.says: An edit stays in the model for every later solve; nothing puts the 1,000 back.

options.text: 700, since three cuts of 10% add up to 30%
options.says: Each 10% is taken of the already-cut limit, so the cuts multiply: 0.9 x 0.9 x 0.9.

options.text: 1,000, since an IncrementalSolver undoes edits after each solve
options.says: An IncrementalSolver sends edits to the solver; it never undoes them. The program must.

questions.heading: Undo Every Edit, and Never Delete What a Scenario Only Switches Off
questions.stem: For one scenario a planner must leave out project P21, whose start variables appear in budget rows and the objective. The next scenario includes P21 again. How should the scenario code leave it out?

options.text: Delete P21's variables, then add them again for the next scenario
options.says: Deleting removes them from every row and the objective, and the old references raise ValueError; adding back means rebuilding those terms.

options.text: Set the upper bound of its variables to 0, then put the old bounds back
options.says: Right: bounding to 0 rules P21 out for one solve, and restoring the bounds leaves no trace, as the P032 scenario showed.

options.text: Set P21's objective coefficients to 0 and leave its variables as they are
options.says: P21 could still be started, spending budget for no value; only its bounds stop it.

options.text: Set the lower bound of its variables to 1, then put the old bounds back
options.says: A lower bound of 1 forces P21 in; to leave it out, its upper bound goes to 0.
